history_boundary.instructions: Choose A or B as the smallest complete useful implementation for the declared finite current-original history reader. Compare permission/secrecy/lifetime/revision/bounds equally; do not treat proposed metadata or advice as implementation evidence.

criteria.A: Use the conservative existing complete-chain lifetime boundary and add only genuine writer-associated optional history metadata containing actual row created/createdBy and original declared secret paths. Reader requires metadata on EVERY entry, validates one complete create-through-current chain, strips the union of every original secret path plus current secrets, projects at current authority and revision. Unsupported legacy/missing/ambiguous/recreated/discontinuous history refuses, never backfilled or guessed. Connect actual canonical CRUD and checked scenario producers, existing Memory/D1/DO persistence and bounded reader. Most economical useful output; narrower supported historical domain, no new durable authority handle or general history framework.
criteria.B: Introduce a new unique nonreused persistent lifetime identity on records AND history, with original secret/schema evidence bound at every genuine writer and migration. Bounded reader selects only that exact lifetime and original/current secret paths under current authority/revision. Can support repeated model/id recreation and partial lifetime retrieval when genuine associations exist; legacy remains unsupported without truthful provenance. Requires new persistent identity/row columns and all writer/migration/backend propagation, a broader representation and qualification change. Better eventual lifetime coverage but greater cost than the conservative complete-chain scope.
